newsitem.title: UK: Euro jet fuel edges up with futures in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Euro jet fuel edges up with futures in slow trade.

text.p: European jet fuel ended stronger on Friday on the back of higher futures.
Premiums were unchanged in a very apathetic market that looks increasingly long, traders said.
May IPE gas oil was trading $2.00 higher at $171.00 at 1616 GMT, near its session high of $171.25.
Barge premiums were holding around May IPE +$20-21 fob ARA while cargoes were lamely holding around June IPE +$21-22 cif NWE.

Dealers said the market's length was in the cargo rather than barge sector, which partly explained the small price discrepancy. In addition the German buy tender would be easier to source from the barge market than from elsewhere.
In the Mediterranean buying was lacklustre.
"If you don't have to buy, then there is no reason to," commented one broker.

Prices for Med material were showing a wide spread with 40,000 tonne cargoes from Greece able to attract as high as fob high quotes +$9 while French and Italian material was $2 below this. Non-EU spec was also under pressure around fob high quotes +$2-3.
